items.description: Identify the report as a systematic review, meta-analysis, or both, and indicate that it addresses health equity.

Structured summary of the review, which includes, as a minimum: background, objectives, data sources, study eligibility criteria, participants, and interventions, study appraisal and synthesis methods, results, limitations, conclusions and implications of key findings, systematic review registration number, and a statement of how the review addresses health equity.
Rationale for the review in the context of what is already known, including a clear statement of the dimension of health equity examined.
Explicit statement of questions being addressed with reference to participants, interventions, comparisons, outcomes, and study design (PICOS), and the dimension of health equity being examined.
Indicate if a review protocol exists, if and where it can be accessed (e.g., Web address), and, if available, provide registration information including registration number.

Specify study characteristics (e.g., PICOS, length of follow-up) and report characteristics (e.g., years considered, language, publication status) used as criteria for eligibility, giving rationale, and indicate the dimension of health equity being examined.
Describe all information sources (e.g., databases with dates of coverage, contact with study authors to identify additional studies) in the search and date last searched.
Present full electronic search strategy for at least one database, including any limits used, such that it could be repeated.

State the process for selecting studies (i.e., screening, eligibility, inclusion in the systematic review, and inclusion in the meta-analysis) and for how the dimension of health equity was considered.

Describe method of data extraction from reports (e.g., piloted forms, independently, in duplicate) and any processes for obtaining and confirming data from investigators, including data related to the dimension of health equity.
List and define all variables for which data were sought (e.g., PICOS, funding sources) and any assumptions and simplifications made, including those related to the dimension of health equity.

Describe methods used for assessing risk of bias of individual studies (including specification of whether this was done at the study or outcome level), and how this information is to be used in any data synthesis, and how the dimension of health equity was considered in this assessment.
State the principal summary measures (e.g., risk ratio, difference in means).

Describe the methods of handling data and combining results of studies, if done, including measures of consistency (e.g., I2) for each meta-analysis, and how the dimension of health equity was considered.
Specify any assessment of risk of bias that may affect the cumulative evidence (e.g., publication bias, selective reporting within studies), and how the dimension of health equity was considered.
Describe methods of additional analyses (e.g., sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression), if done, indicating which were pre-specified, and how the dimension of health equity was considered.

Give flow of studies through the different phases of a systematic review (i.e., numbers of studies screened, assessed for eligibility, and included in the review, with reasons for exclusions at each stage), preferably using a flow diagram, and show how studies that report on the dimension of health equity are included.

For each study, present characteristics for which data were extracted (e.g., study size, PICOS, follow-up period) and provide the citations, including characteristics related to the dimension of health equity.
Present data on risk of bias of each study and, if available, any outcome level assessment, and how the dimension of health equity was considered.

For all outcomes considered (benefits or harms), present, for each study: (a) simple summary data for each intervention group and (b) effect estimates and confidence intervals, ideally with a forest plot, and how the dimension of health equity was considered.
Present results of any other analyses conducted (e.g., sensitivity or subgroup analyses, meta-regression), and how the dimension of health equity was considered.
Present results of any assessment of risk of bias across studies, and how the dimension of health equity was considered.
Summarize the main findings including the strength of evidence for each main outcome; consider their relevance to key groups, including the dimension of health equity.

Discuss limitations at study and outcome level (e.g., risk of bias), and at review-level (e.g., incomplete retrieval of identified research, reporting bias), and how the dimension of health equity was considered.
Provide a general interpretation of the results in the context of other evidence, and implications for future research, taking into account the dimension of health equity.
Describe sources of funding for the systematic review and other support (e.g., supply of data); role of funders for the systematic review.
